# Opening Your Heart to God’s Presence

## Sri Daya Mata — Self-Realization Fellowship

### The Silent Call of the Soul

The deepest yearning of every human heart, whether recognized or unrecognized, is for the unconditional love and comforting presence of our Divine Mother. In the rush and clamor of modern life, the soul often feels isolated, cast adrift on an ocean of temporary experiences and fleeting relationships. Yet, as our beloved Guru, Paramahansa Yogananda, taught us, we are never truly alone. The Divine is closer than our very breath, nearer than our hands and feet. To experience this sacred connection, we must learn the art of opening our hearts—quieting the turbulent waves of the mind so that we may perceive the subtle, loving current of God’s presence within.

Sri Daya Mata, one of the foremost disciples of Paramahansa Yogananda and the third president of Self-Realization Fellowship, shared this timeless truth with unparalleled tenderness and spiritual authority. She reminds us that God is not a distant, judgmental deity sitting in a remote heaven, but the most loving, intimate Friend we could ever have. To feel His presence, we do not need complex intellectual systems; we need only the simplicity of a child’s love.

> "The Lord does not look at your external actions or your intellectual achievements. He looks only at the love of your heart. When you call to Him with the sincerity of a child crying for its mother, He cannot resist your appeal."

### Establishing the Altar of Silence

To begin this journey of opening the heart, we must establish a daily sanctuary of silence. Our thoughts are like restless waves that distort the reflection of the moon on a lake. When we quiet the mind through the sacred techniques of meditation—such as those taught by Self-Realization Fellowship—the water becomes still, and the beautiful image of the Divine is perfectly reflected within our consciousness.

During meditation, let go of all worries, anxieties, and plans for the future. Offer them into the fire of devotion. Sri Daya Mata often emphasized that meditation is not a passive waiting, but an active, dynamic engagement of the soul’s willpower and love. We must knock at the door of the Divine with intense, focused concentration until the door is thrown open.

### Conversing with the Divine Mother

One of the sweetest aspects of Sri Daya Mata's guidance is her instruction on how to talk to God. She encouraged devotees to speak to the Divine Mother in their own words, without formality or pretense. Tell Her your struggles, your joys, your fears, and your hopes.

> "Do not pray to God with empty words. Speak to Him out of the depths of your soul. Say to Him, 'Lord, I want Thee. I seek Thee. Reveal Thyself unto me.' When you speak to Him with this urgency, He will answer you in the silent language of peace, joy, and deep intuitive understanding."

By keeping this constant, silent conversation going throughout the day, we transform our ordinary activities into acts of worship. Whether we are working in an office, cooking a meal, or walking in nature, we can mentally hold the hand of the Divine Mother. This practice of the "Presence of God" guards our hearts against negative emotions and fills our daily life with a steady, quiet joy.

### The Guru's Grace: The Light on the Path

To truly open our hearts, we need the guidance of one who has already crossed the ocean of samsara—a true Guru. Paramahansa Yogananda came to the West to show us the practical, scientific path of Kriya Yoga, which directly leads to the perception of God's presence. Sri Daya Mata, who lived in the Master’s presence for over twenty years, witnessed firsthand the transformative power of his divine love.

She often spoke of how the Guru’s gaze could melt the hardest heart, revealing the pure, unblemished soul underneath. The Guru acts as a mirror, reflecting our own divine nature back to us, and encouraging us to cast away the rags of ego-limitation. By tuning in to the Guru’s consciousness through devotion and obedience to his teachings, we receive the spiritual grace necessary to quiet our restless minds and open our hearts fully to the Divine Mother.

> "The Guru is the human vehicle through whom God reaches out to the seeking soul. When you align your will with the Guru's guidance, his grace flows into your life, dissolving the ancient karmic barriers that have kept you separated from your Beloved."

### Finding God in Times of Trial

It is easy to feel God's presence when our lives are smooth and peaceful. However, Sri Daya Mata taught us that the true test of our devotion comes during times of trial, physical suffering, or emotional distress. It is in these moments of darkness that we must cling most desperately to the hem of the Divine Mother's garment.

Instead of complaining or asking "Why me?", we should look upon trials as opportunities to deepen our surrender. Every difficulty we face is a sacred challenge, designed to strip away our reliance on the outer world and force us to seek our security solely in the changeless Divine Spirit. When we face our trials with courage, faith, and a loving heart, we find that the Divine Mother is right there, holding us in Her arms, whispering words of comfort and strength.

> "Do not let the storms of life shake your inner peace. Keep your anchor deep in the ocean of God's love. Remember that this world is but a cosmic dream, and your only true reality is your eternal relationship with Him."

### Cultivating the Quality of Surrender

True devotion requires surrender—not a weak giving up of our will, but the alignment of our human will with the Divine Will. Sri Daya Mata taught that when we surrender our lives to God, we are placing our small, limited selves into the hands of Infinite Wisdom. We must trust that whatever comes to us in life is a gift from His hand, designed to help our souls grow and realize our oneness with Him.

This attitude of surrender frees us from the heavy burden of egoic worry. We no longer ask, "What will happen to me?" but instead declare, "Lord, Thy will be done. I am Thine, and Thou art mine. Guide me, protect me, and let Thy love flow through me to all whom I meet."

### Daily Spiritual Habits for Opening the Heart

To help you integrate these teachings into your daily life, here are practical, step-by-step spiritual habits:

*   **Begin and End Your Day with God:** Before you rise in the morning and before you fall asleep at night, offer your first and last thoughts to the Divine Mother. Pray, "Lord, my day is Thine; guide my actions," and "Lord, into Thy hands I commend my spirit."
*   **Practice Silent Interiorized Meditation:** Set aside dedicated time each day for silent meditation. Use the techniques taught by the Guru to quiet the body and mind, and then sit in the deep stillness, feeling the warmth of divine love in your heart.
*   **Speak to Him in Your Own Language:** Do not use rote prayers. Talk to God as your dearest Friend. Express your heart's devotion simply, sincerely, and continuously.
*   **Perform Daily Acts of Kindness:** Serve others with the understanding that the same Divine Presence dwells in them. Let your love for God manifest as selfless service and kindness to those around you.
*   **Cultivate Spiritual Cheerfulness:** Keep your mind anchored in positivity and joy. Remind yourself that you are a child of God, and nothing in this world can harm your immortal soul.

### A Prayer for Divine Union

Let us close our minds to the outer world for a moment and go deep within the sacred chamber of our hearts. Let us pray together:

"O Divine Mother, Lord of the Universe, my beloved Guru! Fill my heart with Thy love. Let me feel Thy presence in every breath, in every thought, and in every beat of my heart. Wash away all shadows of doubt, fear, and restlessness. Reveal Thyself unto me as the ultimate Love, the ultimate Peace, and the ultimate Joy. I am Thine, Lord. Keep me ever nestled in Thy loving embrace. 

Jai Guru. Jai Ma."
